reasons: Classification is correct: Section 4.1 has an automatic one-year (not multi-year) renewal, but the ninety (90) day non-renewal/termination notice window exceeds the fallback ceiling of 60 days on a material term, so it is a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback; it is also correctly characterised as short of walk-away territory (>90 days).

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position: only 'ninety (90)' becomes 'thirty (30)' (changed-character ratio 0.089), leaving the 12-month renewal term intact, which already matches the preferred position.

The comment accurately states what changed and why, cites the 30-day opt-out on 12-month renewals position, and offers the 60-day fallback in the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.

The rationale properly relegates the absent 60-day vendor reminder and the absence of any renewal repricing/uplift language to notes rather than treating them as separate deviations, consistent with the minor sub-element convention.

Minor point for negotiation, not a defect in the finding: the notice right is mutual, so shortening it to 30 days also lets HDI exit faster; if continuity matters, consider an asymmetric window (Customer 30 days, Vendor unchanged).
